tasks.title: fix(ui): remove the non-OO blue focus ring around the editor content surface
tasks.accept: cd apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg && timeout 300 /usr/bin/node --test *.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qE '^# (tests|pass) ' && timeout 300 /usr/bin/node --test *.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -Eq '^# fail 0$'
tasks.acceptance_prose: The #editor:focus box-shadow rule is gone from style.css and the full test suite passes with 0 failures.
tasks.note:
VERIFIED FACT (live 2026-11-15): OO's document editor draws NO box-shadow/outline ring around the content/viewer surface on focus. Live probe of the OO demo (onlyoffice 9.4.0, world-office.graphwiz.ai/demo, frameEditor iframe): computed style of #id_viewer = box-shadow:none, outline:none; a blue-halo scan (every element >=300x300 with a bluish box-shadow) returned ZERO hits. OO's focus signal is the text caret + canvas selection highlight, NOT a shell ring.

WO currently has this rule in apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg/style.css:
    #editor:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--accent); }

It draws a 2px rgb(55,96,143) frame around the whole 1648x746 #editor scroll surface (all pages + empty backdrop) whenever the editor gets focus. This is (a) wrong vs OO and (b) reads as a bug: the ring spans the entire canvas area and clips/pulses while typing/selecting.

TASK: delete that exact rule (the line `#editor:focus { box-shadow: ... }`). Do NOT add a replacement ring/outline on #editor, .wo-page, or the canvas. Do NOT touch the ::selection styling, the caret, @media print rules, or anything else. The editor already has role="textbox" + aria-label so accessibility is intact without the ring.

Also verify no other rule targets #editor with a focus box-shadow/outline (grep 'editor:focus' and '#editor.*focus'). Commit only style.css. The test suite must stay at # fail 0 (currently 158 tests, 0 fail). There is no test asserting this ring today (verified: no test greps for editor:focus box-shadow), so removing it cannot break a gate.

tasks.acceptance_prose: ctx-parity.test.mjs exists and passes; full suite stays at 0 failures; plain-text right-click shows only OO's text-menu rows in OO order.
tasks.note:
VERIFIED FACTS (OO 9.4.0, live + source) — OO's TEXT context menu (right-click on paragraph text, no object/table/spell/revision):

OO visible rows, in order (German labels observed live):
  1. (spell block, ONLY when a misspelled word is at the caret: suggestion / Ignore / Ignore all / ▸ Select language — WO already gates these via data-showif="misspelled", KEEP IT)
  2. Cut, 3. Copy, 4. Paste
  5. Print selection
  6. Seite vorumbruch / Page break before (WO: PageBreakBefore)
  7. Absatz zusammenhalten / Keep lines together (WO: KeepLines)
  8. Absatz - Erweiterte Einstellungen / Paragraph advanced settings (WO: ParagraphSettings)
  9. Kommentar hinzufügen / Add comment (WO: AddComment)
 10. Link (WO: Link)
 11. Formatierung als Formatvorlage / Formatting as style (WO: FormattingAsStyle)
 12. AI (submenu)

CRITICAL: OO's text menu DOES NOT contain, on plain text: Undo, Redo, Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough, clear formatting, TextDirection, lists (bullet/numbered/start-new/continue/setvalue/listindents/bullets&numbering), horizontal rule, caption, footnote, endnote, symbol, date, page number, UpdateTOC, field codes, AcceptChange, RejectChange, dropcap/frame/equation/content-control settings. OO's pictureMenu (image selected) and tableMenu (table cell) and shape menus are SEPARATE scenarios shown only in those contexts. The CHARACTER FORMATTING block (bold/italic/underline/strikeout) never appears in OO's text menu even with a selection — confirmed twice live: right-click on plain text and on a selected word produce the SAME 15-row (or 12-row clean) menu.

WO's current markup (index.html id="ctx-menu") has 74 data-ctx rows; the following are currently ALWAYS visible (no data-showif) and MUST become hidden on plain text:
  - Undo, Redo (formatting block)
  - Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeThrough, RemoveFormat
  - TextDirection + TextDirHorizontal/RotateDown/RotateUp
  - AI submenu rows are fine to keep gated to AI group
  - BulletList, NumberedList, StartNewList, ContinueNumbering, SetNumberingValue, AdjustListIndents, BulletsAndNumbering
  - HorizontalRule, HorizontalLineSettings, Caption, Footnote, Endnote, Symbol, Date, PageNumber
  - UpdateTOC, TocSettings, UpdateField, EditField, ToggleFieldCodes, PageBreakBefore(keep visible!), AcceptChange, RejectChange
  - DropcapSettings, FrameSettings, EquationSettings, ContentControlSettings, RemoveContentControl
  - PrintSelection, SelectAll

APPROACH (do NOT delete any data-ctx buttons — existing tests (ctx-menu.test.mjs, ctx-convert-to-shape, ctx-distribute-*, ctx-edit-*, etc.) assert >=20 data-ctx buttons exist, each has a Ctx.* i18n key, and each is handled in the editor.js dispatcher; deleting buttons BREAKS those tests. Instead:
1. In index.html give every row that OO hides on plain text a data-showif attribute with the correct context name: formatting rows (Undo/Redo/Bold/Italic/Underline/StrikeThrough/RemoveFormat) -> data-showif="format"; list rows -> data-showif="list"; insert rows (HorizontalRule..PageNumber) -> data-showif="insert-ctx" or keep them but gate to a context that is FALSE on plain paragraph text; TextDirection rows -> data-showif="shapetext" (OO shows text-direction only inside shapes); AcceptChange/RejectChange -> data-showif="trackchanges"; UpdateTOC/TocSettings -> data-showif="toc"; UpdateField/EditField/ToggleFieldCodes -> data-showif="field"; DropcapSettings -> data-showif="dropcap"; FrameSettings -> data-showif="frame"; EquationSettings -> data-showif="equation"; ContentControlSettings/RemoveContentControl -> data-showif="control". Pick sensible names; the existing ctx-menu.test.mjs checks data-showif attributes exist on advanced-settings rows and that the build step refreshes them — keep collab-dialogs/consistency-gate happy.
2. In editor.js contextmenu handler (around L11372-11470, function attached to editorEl 'contextmenu'), compute the NEW contexts: hasSelection (window.getSelection() not collapsed), inList (selectionIsInList() — implement: walk ancestors of selection anchorNode for OL/UL or elements with data-listid), inTOC (closest .toc-container or [data-field=sdt] / data-field with fieldKind TOC), inField (existing ctxNode logic already gates data-showif='field'), hasObjectSelection (existing selectedObject / selectedObjects), canRevise (trackChangesOn for Accept/Reject — already gated). Then set el.hidden = !ctx[name] for every [data-showif] in the menu.
3. Ensure on a PLAIN paragraph right-click (no selection, no table, no object, no spell, no revision) the visible rows are EXACTLY, in this order: Cut, Copy, Paste, [sep], PrintSelection, PageBreakBefore, KeepLines, ParagraphSettings, [sep], AddComment, Link, [sep], FormattingAsStyle, AI. (numerical x/order = DOM order in #ctx-menu; if the DOM order differs you may REORDER those rows in index.html to match; keep all buttons present.) Use the existing hidden/hide() mechanism (ctxMenu.querySelectorAll + el.hidden) already used for misspelled/table/object.
4. ADD apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg/ctx-parity.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert, zero deps, reads index.html + editor.js source): (a) assert the plain-text visible set from DOM order — extract the ordered list of data-ctx values that have NO data-showif and whose data-showif context is false-by-default, and assert it equals [Cut,Copy,Paste,PrintSelection,PageBreakBefore,KeepLines,ParagraphSettings,AddComment,Link,FormattingAsStyle,AI] in that relative order; (b) assert Undo/Redo/Bold/Italic/Underline/StrikeThrough/RemoveFormat/BulletList/NumberedList/HorizontalRule/Caption/Footnote/Endnote/Symbol/Date/PageNumber/TextDirection/UpdateTOC/UpdateField/DropcapSettings/FrameSettings/EquationSettings/ContentControlSettings/AcceptChange/RejectChange each carry a data-showif OR a JS gating line in editor.js (at minimum assert they are NOT in the always-visible list computed in (a)); (c) assert editor.js handler has code setting el.hidden from the new contexts (grep for 'data-showif' loop). Test must pass standalone: `node --test ctx-parity.test.mjs`.

Constraint: full suite `timeout 300 /usr/bin/node --test *.test.mjs` must stay # fail 0. Do NOT remove any data-ctx button, do NOT change Ctx.* i18n keys, do NOT break the dispatcher switch. Keep diff boring.

tasks.title: capture: ctx-scenarios.cjs — scenario walker that right-clicks each interaction context (text/selection/table/image/shape/misspelled/field/toc/tracked-changes) on WO and OO and emits normalized visible-row JSON per scenario
tasks.acceptance_prose: ctx-scenarios.cjs parses and its --self mode runs green; the walker is wired for WO+OO live capture.
tasks.note:
Build the systematic scenario walker that the research prescribed (wo-test-harness/census/RESEARCH-CAPTURE-ALL.md, section 4A). It must be a self-contained /usr/bin/node CJS script using the already-installed playwright at /home/weiss/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs (require it; do not add npm deps). Reuse the proven capture recipe from census/chrome-census2.cjs (viewports, waits, iframe handling).

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR:
- Provides `--self` mode: no network, just prints 'SELF-OK' (used by the acceptance gate).
- Default mode (live): opens WO editor at https://editor.cloud.graphwiz.ai/word/ (viewport 1680x950, locale de-DE, wait ~6s after domcontentloaded) and the OO demo reference at https://world-office.graphwiz.ai/demo (viewport 1760x950; click the .file 'Bericht.docx' entry; wait ~15-20s for the editor; widen the frameEditor iframe to 1680x950 via injected style 'iframe[name="frameEditor"] { width: 1680px !important; height: 950px !important; }' and wait ~3s; find the frame named frameEditor and wait for its .toolbar).
- For the WO side, for each scenario below, position the mouse, right-click, read the #ctx-menu visible buttons (offsetParent !== null / el.hidden === false) in order (text + data-ctx), collapse, move on:
  scenarios: text (right-click x=800 y=500 paragraph area), selection (select a word first via dblclick / keyboard, then right-click), misspelled (only if a misspell exists), table (insert a table via the Insert ribbon if available or skip with note), image (skip with note if Bericht.docx has none), field (skip if none), toc (skip if none), trackchanges-on (toggle via Review ribbon if available).
- For the OO side, right-click inside the widened frameEditor at the same coordinates, collect the OS menu (menu-item / .menu-item / .dropdown-submenu elements visible, ordered by y), map captions to best-effort canonical names.
- Emit, to stdout and to census/ctx-scenarios.json, one normalized record per scenario per engine:
  { "scenario": "text", "engine": "wo" | "oo", "rows": [ {"key": "Cut", "caption": "Ausschneiden"} ... ] } — for WO derive key from data-ctx; for OO use a best-effort canonical key from the caption (keep an ooRawCaption field).
- On network/load failure of either engine, print a clear NOTICE line and continue (never hang; wrap every wait with a try/catch and a sane timeout). Exit 0 if at least one engine was captured.
- Do NOT commit any captured JSON, API keys, or screenshots. Commit only census/ctx-scenarios.cjs.
- Keep the file boring: one file, no classes unless needed, no extra deps, no README.
